text: Soulstealer is an Affliction warlock artifact trait. It is not linked to any other trait and requires all base traits to be learned.

Souldrained Refugees are dead Zandalari trolls strewn about some central and southwestern areas of the Port of Zem'lan in Vol'dun. At least some of them are the remains of troll refugees that were killed by Pirate-King Zem'lan when attempting to seek refuge on his ships from a Faithless attack ages ago.

Soulspitter Cobras are serpents that accompany Basher Hak'anjin, Bun'zia the Hacker, Gunner Zol'jabu, Lookout Rakana, Lookout Ungalra, Master Gunner Garna, Tamer Dukazi, Tamer Khuwaza, Tamer Sejuuma, Umbo the Sneak, and Zuk'su in the Port of Zem'lan in Vol'dun.
Soultainted Cobras are large serpents mostly found burrowing underground in the western outskirts of the Port of Zem'lan in Vol'dun. They are also seen accompanying Tamer Gonja and Tamer Zalo'bin.

Souldrained Invaders are sethrak corpses that litter the northern outskirts of the Port of Zem'lan in Vol'dun. They are ostensibly the remains of the Faithless invaders who attacked the port ages ago.

Souldrained Defenders are dead Zandalari trolls strewn about the northern outskirts of the Port of Zem'lan in Vol'dun, as well as Nim'ra the Facestomper's area in the southeastern part of the port. They are apparently the remains of members of Pirate-King Zem'lan's crew who attempted to hold off a Faithless assault ages ago.

Spam (in the electronic sense, not the food) has several definitions according to context, mostly derogatory. All share the key property of excessive repetition, either over time or across multiple subjects. "Spamming" is the act of generating spam, and "spammers" are those who do so.

The Sparklematic 5200 is a slot-machine-like contraption in The Clean Zone of Gnomeregan, used to wash the grime off of Grime-Encrusted Objects. A plaque on it reads: "Grime and residue ruining your sparklies? The Sparklematic 5200 puts the shine back in shine-tastic! Insert the item you wish to clean and deposit three silver coins in the coin slot. Give the Sparklematic 5200 a moment for operation, and voila! Your valuables will emerge clean and shiny!" The Sparklematic offers a quest (The Sparklematic 5200! structures after the Cataclysm.]] The Southern Savage Coast is a portion of the Great Sea around the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, mostly noted by travelers on the southwest coast of the Cape of Stranglethorn near Booty Bay. The border between the Savage Coast and its southern namesake lies due south of Grom'gol Base Camp across the bay. After the reawakening of the Dragon Isles, Captain Grub Redcut's ship was docked here.

Southpoint Tower was a ruined scout tower at the far west end of Hillsbrad Foothills, just south of the road to Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken Deathstalker Lesh was stationed there, spying on the Alliance activity in the area. Lesh was often killed by Alliance players because of her secluded position. Before Patch 2.1, this area, as well as Hillsbrad Fields nearby, was accessible to players who explored the Old Hillsbrad Foothills instance in the Caverns of Time. This tower was not ruined in the instance, nor was the unnamed tower between Tarren Mill and Southshore. There was also a gate further down the road, blocking the road to Silverpine Forest. South Tide's Run is complementary to North Tide's Run, and is the name for the southwestern coast of Silverpine Forest bordering the Great Sea. Although not as famous as the northern coast, which is the site of a sunken ship and of great significance to tauren druids, South Tide's Run used to be a popular bathing spot for the humans of Gilneas and Pyrewood. Since the Cataclysm, the land has risen a great deal in this area, causing the area to be short cliffs, rather than a nice shoreline.

This trade route is named for the trade caravans that travel regularly along the highway. Officially, the section of the road that bears the name Southern Gold Road begins at the Great Lift at the southern end of the Barrens and ends at the bridge connecting the northern and southern ends of the Barrens. North of here, the road is simply known as the Gold Road. The road is traveled by traders and adventurers alike, hailing from regions as distant as Gadgetzan in Tanaris Desert and Auberdine in Darkshore, and Nighthaven in the north.

The Southshore Town Hall was an important structure to the remnants of Lordaeron for the time between the Third War and the Cataclysm. Magistrate Henry Maleb was Southshore's ruler, and held office in the building. Kundric Zanden was also here. The town hall and the rest of the town were left in ruins by the Forsaken plague bombing when they achieved victory in the Battle for Hillsbrad. Magistrate Maleb fled to Fenris Isle, and the town hall is now occupied by slime creatures left over from the plague toxins, including Chet the Slime-Breeder.

The Southsea Holdfast is a Southsea Pirates outpost located on a shelf above the Shimmering Deep in Thousand Needles. They've built ramps from the top to the waters down below where they have three vessels awaiting orders. This group of pirates is led by Tony Two-Tusk, which can be found in the nearby cavern named the Admiral's Den. A goblin and his gnome companion from the speedbarge came to this location to barter with the pirate, however, they were captured and since then the pirate have begun attacking the ship. During the Thousand Boat Bash, the ships anchored here are raided for grog. After the Fourth War, the area is still occupied by the Southsea pirates.

The Southern Barrens is a neutral zone for level 30-35 Horde and Alliance players. It focuses on the Alliance vs. Horde conflict, with each faction's quests giving a different view of the events that play out. The progress for the storyline is tracked in the achievement Southern Barrens Quests. The Southern Barrens quests lead to the Dustwallow Marsh storyline; Feralas and Western Plaguelands are same-level alternatives.

Bottles of Southsea Firebrew are found on the pirate ship just offshore of Croaking Hollow, and also near the rowboat that has landed on the shore of the hollow. Drinking some brew provides Timeless Nutriment, instantly healing for 20% of total health and increasing all stats by 5% for 10 minutes.

Southshore vs Tarren Mill (SS vs TM), also referred to as Tarren Mill vs Southshore (TM vs SS), is a 40vs40, "team deathmatch-style" battleground, released as part of World of Warcrafts 10-year anniversary event. It is only available for a limited time, although it may return again at a later point. The battleground is available in two brackets: level 100, and levels 90-99. As well as the usual currencies, winning the battleground will reward a faction-specific title: Tarren Mill Terror for Alliance players and Southshore Slayer for Horde players. Southport is an Alliance settlement in the Spires of Arak. The only major building in this outpost is decided on the commander, which is either the Smuggler's Den or the Stoktron Brewery. Before a choice is made, the space is occupied by Southport Worksite. Once the quest-line is completed, a monument for Admiral Taylor is built.

Sparks of Tyr are mysterious artifacts used by the titanic watcher Tyr to, in his own words, "ensure some future." They are described as being octagonal in shape and made with a strange metal, with a surface that seems to change from iron to golden depending on how they are held. The Sparks of Tyr can record events and replay them within the minds of others.

The Spark of Light is located at the Sanctuary of Light in Netherlight Temple. It was recovered from Hyrja in the Halls of Valor by a priest adventurer, at the urging of Alonsus Faol who believed that it was necessary for the Light to "walk among us". However, it needs infusions of Light from places that are considered especially holy on Azeroth before it can fulfill its potential. It is referred to as a wisp.
